questions.question: Two containers have mixtures of milk and water, respectively, in the ratios 3 ∶ 2 and 6 ∶ 5. In what ratio should the contents be mixed so that the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture is 4 ∶ 3?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27ab83c699d806e3ce36baa6ef583e9bbda077f1db8923684d5dfd3515d20008.png] 

∴ In 10 : 11 the contents should be mixed so that the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture is 4 ∶ 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Two containers have mixtures of milk and water, respectively, in the ratios 3 ∶ 2 and 6 ∶ 5.

The ratio of milk to water in the final mixture is 4 : 3.

Concept used:

Ratio Proportion

Calculation:

Let P unit of the first mixture is added to Q unit of the second mixture.

So, in P unit of first mixture,

Amount of milk present = 3/5 × P = 3P/5

Amount of water present = 2/5 × P = 2P/5

So, in Q unit of second mixture,

Amount of milk present = 6/11 × Q = 6Q/11

Amount of water present = 5/11 × Q = 5Q/11

According to the question,

(3P/5 + 6Q/11) ÷ (2P/5 + 5Q/11) = 4 ÷ 3

⇒ {(33P + 30Q)/55} ÷ {(22P + 25Q)/55} = 4 ÷ 3

⇒ 99P + 90Q = 88P + 100Q

⇒ 11P = 10Q

⇒ P : Q = 10 : 11

**∴ In 10 : 11 the contents should be mixed so that the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture is 4 ∶ 3.**

questions.concept: To Make a Mixture from Two Mixtures
questions.question: Two beakers contain acid and water in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 and 3 ∶ 4 respectively. If equal volumes of the mixtures from these two beakers are poured into a common beaker, find the resultant ration of acid to water in the mixture in the common beaker.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total parts in Beaker 1 = 2 + 3 = 5, and in Beaker 2 = 3 + 4 = 7.

To equalize the volumes directly, multiply Beaker 1 ratio parts by 7 and Beaker 2 ratio parts by 5.

Equated acid and water parts = (14 : 21) for Beaker 1, and (15 : 20) for Beaker 2.

Mixing them directly ⇒ Acid : Water = (14 + 15) : (21 + 20) = 29 : 41.

**∴ The correct answer is 29 : 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of acid to water in Beaker 1 = 2 : 3

Ratio of acid to water in Beaker 2 = 3 : 4

Both beakers contribute equal volumes to the final common mixture.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of Beaker 1 in terms of ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts.

⇒ Total capacity of Beaker 2 in terms of ratio parts = 3 + 4 = 7 parts.

⇒ Let the equal volume taken from both beakers be the LCM of 5 and 7, which is 35 units.

⇒ In Beaker 1, quantity of acid = (2 ÷ 5) × 35 = 14 units.

⇒ In Beaker 1, quantity of water = (3 ÷ 5) × 35 = 21 units.

⇒ In Beaker 2, quantity of acid = (3 ÷ 7) × 35 = 15 units.

⇒ In Beaker 2, quantity of water = (4 ÷ 7) × 35 = 20 units.

⇒ When poured together into the common beaker, Total Acid = 14 + 15 = 29 units.

⇒ When poured together into the common beaker, Total Water = 21 + 20 = 41 units.

⇒ The resultant ratio of acid to water in the final mixture = 29 : 41.

**∴ The correct answer is 29 : 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixtures in Unequal Volumes

If two mixtures are combined in a specific ratio of volumes (m : n), first equalize the total parts of their respective internal ratios, then multiply them by m and n before adding the corresponding components together.

Replacement Method

When a certain volume of a mixture is removed and replaced by one of its pure components, the ratio of the remaining original mixture stays unchanged right before the pure component is added.

Rule of Alligation

It helps determine the exact ratio in which two mixtures should be mixed to achieve a desired final concentration: Quantity of cheaper ÷ Quantity of dearer = (Cost of dearer − Mean price) ÷ (Mean price − Cost of cheaper).

questions.question: In what ratio must tea at Rs. 58 per kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 64 per kg so that the mixture must be worth Rs. 60 per kg?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tea at Rs. 58 per kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 64 per kg,

CP of the mixture must be worth Rs. 60 per kg.

**Calculation:**

Let x kg of tea at Rs 58 per kg be mixed with y kg of tea at Rs. 64 per kg .

According to the question,

58x + 64y = (x + y) × 60

⇒ 58x + 64y = 60x + 60y

⇒ 60x - 58x = 64y - 60y

⇒ 2x = 4y

⇒ x = 2y

So, the ratio should be x : y = 2 : 1

**∴ The required ratio is 2 : 1**

questions.question: In what ratio should rice worth Rs. 140 per kg and Rs. 90 per kg be mixed so that & mixture of two qualities of rice may become worth Rs. 110 per kg?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By using the direct rule of Alligation:

Ratio of Quantities = (Mean − Price₂) : (Price₁ − Mean)

⇒ Ratio = (110 − 90) : (140 − 110)

⇒ Ratio = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of Type 1 rice = ₹140 per kg

Price of Type 2 rice = ₹90 per kg

Mean price of the mixture = ₹110 per kg

**Formula Used:**

Mean Price = (Price₁ × Qty₁ + Price₂ × Qty₂) ÷ (Qty₁ + Qty₂)

**Calculation:**

Let the required ratio of Type 1 to Type 2 rice be x : y.

⇒ 110 = (140 × x + 90 × y) ÷ (x + y)

⇒ 110 × (x + y) = 140x + 90y

⇒ 110x + 110y = 140x + 90y

⇒ 110y − 90y = 140x − 110x

⇒ 20y = 30x

⇒ x / y = 20 / 30

⇒ x : y = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a quick cross-multiplication method used to find the ratio in which two substances must be mixed to achieve a desired mean price. The ratio of the quantity of the dearer to the cheaper substance is always evaluated as (Mean Price − Cheaper Price) : (Dearer Price − Mean Price).

Replacement Method

If a vessel initially contains 'a' liters of pure liquid, and 'b' liters is removed and replaced with water 'n' times in succession, the remaining quantity of pure liquid in the final mixture is given by a × (1 − b/a)ⁿ.

Weighted Average

The mean price of a mixture can also be calculated directly using the standard weighted average formula: Mean = (Q₁ × P₁ + Q₂ × P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂).

questions.question: In what ratio must a shopkeeper mix sugar at ₹30/kg and ₹32.5/kg so that by selling the mixture at ₹34.1/kg, he may get 10% profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of sugar type 1 = ₹30/kg

Cost price of sugar type 2 = ₹32.5/kg

Selling price of the mixture = ₹34.1/kg

Profit = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = (1 + Profit%) × Cost Price

Using the Rule of Allegation:

Ratio = (Cost Price of type 2 - Mean Price) : (Mean Price - Cost Price of type 1)
